Image1 is the EDIT TARGET: preserve this exact REAR camera, perspective, full-body framing, same muscular man, head, torso, supported chest, pelvis, legs, feet, chair, fixed machine tower/post/beam/pivot housings, floor, colors and lighting. This is the wide-open end of a bilateral REVERSE PEC DECK FLY. Change ONLY BOTH ARMS and their attached moving machine levers to a clear STARTING position for the same rear-delt fly. Do not rotate the body or camera.
START POSITION: Both arms point diagonally FORWARD AWAY FROM THE VIEWER at shoulder height, with each arm ALREADY ABOUT20DEGREES OPEN LATERALLY from straight forward. This modest pre-opening makes both upper arms, elbows and forearms visible in this camera, while retaining a large further opening range before the T endpoint of the edit target. Hands are moderately separated, just wider than shoulders, much closer together than in Image1.
CRITICAL ANATOMY: maintain the SMALL about10degree elbow bend of Image1. Arms must be ALMOST STRAIGHT from shoulder through elbow to wrist; they must NOT fold into a U, NOT have elbows bent90degrees, and NOT look like rowing or pressing. ALL articulation comes from horizontal rotation at the shoulders, not elbow flexion. Because the camera is elevated and the arms point forward into depth, both elbows must project slightly UPWARD AND OUTWARD from the shoulders, then the wrists project farther UPWARD AND OUTWARD on almost the same line. LEFT visible arm: shoulder -> elbow up/left -> wrist farther up/left, nearly a straight diagonal. RIGHT arm: shoulder -> elbow up/right -> wrist farther up/right, nearly a straight diagonal. Absolutely no elbow hanging DOWN below the shoulder while the hand points upward; that would be a wrong folded-arm pose. Leave the elbow joints slightly soft, not hyperextended.
Both hands hold the original vertical grips. Rotate the SAME TWO rigid levers at their overhead pivots into their forward/start positions so the grips follow the forward hands. Do not invent new machine pieces, bend the support, lose a post or float a grip. Keep the full fixed frame exactly as in Image1. The man's head/upper back/torso/hips/feet stay in the EXACT same place; back remains naturally supported against the chest pad, no shrug, no torso twist. Only arms/levers differ. Show arms forward with all major joints clearly linked and the required large opening still available. No extra limbs, text, arrows or motion trails. Color, skin and clothing match Image1.
